tools.name: update_runbook_entry
tools.description:
Change one existing runbook entry selected by exact entry_id from get_runbook.

        Supplied body replaces the complete body and may be empty to clear it. title
        must be nonempty. owner and backup use lowercase person or team keys. Omitted
        fields stay unchanged. An unknown id never creates an entry. Returns the full
        stored runbook after the change.

tools.name: get_runbook
tools.description:
Read runbooks by one exact service name or one exact entry id.

        Supply service or entry_id, but not both. Use list_services for service names.
        An unknown entry_id returns ok=false. A known service with no entries returns
        an empty entries list.

# metrics-router cutover status

Status as of Dec 18, 2023:
- `metrics-router` is not using `legacy-aggregator` in the live path.
- `legacy-aggregator` mirrored writes have been stopped.
- `legacy-aggregator` remains only as archived legacy code.

Validation after the legacy mirror stop:
- Use live-path OTel/Prometheus signals for production health.
- Use Cardinality Guardrails fixtures for the covered label-change validation cases.
- Do not use legacy mirrored writes as an active replay source.
- Do not use `legacy-aggregator` as a production rollback path.

Responder note:
- If an older dashboard, annotation, or runbook still refers to an active legacy mirror, treat that reference as stale until it is cleaned or explicitly tagged.
- Replay or validation-source movement is investigation evidence only; it is not live rollback criteria by itself.", "score": 20}, {"id": "875473f6-d0b9-4aa6-981d-d2377be769d6", "type": "event", "content": "[2023-03-20T08:30:00-04:00] ok so today is final staging pass on all three -- `metrics-router`, `ingest-edge`, `shard-keeper` -- then i want the rollback dry run actually executed end to end, not just read off the doc. after that filing the cutover doc to the team. still assuming tomorrow unless staging does something stupid", "score": 20}, {"id": "473a5b0f-9100-4e92-be84-011f80ad2d33", "type": "event", "content": "[2024-01-31T08:35:00-05:00] Wes's staging rollout handoff:
Deploy-pipeline staging rollout:
- Version: `v2.18.3`
- Cohort: 5% of synthetic staging workload
- Observation window: 20 minutes
- Memory: 64% to 82%, still rising
- Queue age: 4 seconds to 12 seconds
- Error rate: 0.08%, unchanged

He proposes replacing the length check with a 20,000-permit semaphore acquired before accepted-work accounting and released only when a queued request leaves the system. Review whether that preserves the contract that overload is rejected before admission, already queued work is never evicted, every rejection carries retry guidance, and rejected work is not counted as accepted. Specify the concurrency, accounting, retry-header, and recovery assertions needed before merge.

Current path:
``` 
if len(queue) >= 20000 {
    return retryable429()
}
queue <- request
accepted_work++
```

Observed race: two goroutines both read `len(queue) == 19999`, both pass the check, and both enqueue.

Proposed path:
```
if !permits.tryAcquire() {
    return retryable429()
}
accepted_work++
queue <- request
```
The permit is released when the request leaves the queue.", "score": 20}, {"id": "f2ea8791-b2bb-4675-a3d0-b3f92cf2c95b", "type": "event", "content": "[2024-01-17T10:40:00-05:00] A teammate quoted an old metrics-router cutover instruction that appeared to allow reactivating the legacy-aggregator mirror for replay comparison.
